name: lineage survives an async boundary
why: Python copies the context at asyncio.create_task and TypeScript's AsyncLocalStorage follows await, so an SDK should get this free — but only if the binding lives somewhere that participates in that machinery rather than on the client object or in the coroutine's arguments. This is also the only case that runs the async client path, a separate code path in both languages. What it deliberately does NOT claim to catch, having been mutation-tested against it: a thread-local standing in for a context-local. Sequential calls cannot tell those apart, because each one sets and clears before the next begins; only two interleaved tasks holding different bindings can, and expressing that needs concurrency this declarative schema cannot carry without making record order racy. That property is pinned by each SDK's own tests (Python: tests/test_propagation.py). A concurrent step group with order-insensitive matching is the corpus-side upgrade path.
